strategy_policy.ratio_selection: Existing 260-week INTC/SPY equity beta through 2026-10-30, fixed before this payoff calculation. Not the asset beta used in the DCF.
strategy_policy.capital: Fully fund SPY long plus own cash buffer plus opening transaction costs. Short proceeds remain separate. No margin loan funds the SPY purchase.
strategy_policy.rebalancing: None; fixed initial long and short shares, with SPY distributions reinvested. Initial beta matching does not maintain market neutrality as prices/betas change.
strategy_policy.index_return_basis: 4.94% paired NYU Treasury plus 4.41% implied ERP. Using this as a constant finite-horizon total-return CAGR is an additional explicit assumption.
strategy_policy.net_short_yield_basis: Illustrative aggregate net yield after borrow/program costs, not an actual INTC quote. Current posted marginal short-proceeds tiers and large-account scale make it a useful control, not a secured future rate.
strategy_policy.cash_yield_basis: Current IBKR Pro marginal normal USD cash rate, used as a constant scenario; tier blending, eligibility and future changes not forecast.
strategy_policy.hurdle_basis: Reference opportunity-cost hurdle from the paired NYU Treasury input. It is not asserted to be a locked 3-5-year cash return or the broker rebate. Also compare against identical broker-cash yield and show hurdle sensitivity.
strategy_policy.transaction_cost_basis: Explicit illustrative 10bp on opening and closing gross leg notionals, not a broker quote. Opening fees add to required investor capital; closing fees use terminal leg values.
strategy_policy.Intel_dividends: None, consistent with the retained-cash forecast. Introducing dividends requires reducing retained terminal cash and adding short payments jointly.
strategy_policy.interpretation: A specified buy-and-hold relative allocation with initial beta matching. Conditional terminal wealth and capital comparisons, not demonstrated expected alpha or a guarantee of sufficient margin in every interim path.
strategy_policy.tier_blend_meaning: At the observed posted schedule, ($0.1m*0+$0.9m*2.63%+$2m*3.38%+$7m*3.63%)/$10m = 3.4537% before stock borrow/program charges. This is a current schedule illustration, not an executable INTC quote or a locked future net yield.

formula.original_capital: K = H + M + c*(H+S), with H=beta*S and M=S. Opening transaction costs are paid from additional own capital.
formula.comparison: Compare W with K*(1+capital_hurdle)^T. Also compare with identical initial SPY allocation and remaining cash, omitting the Intel short.
formula.notional_normalization: Results per $100 initial Intel short; strategy policy scales that to $10M.

adjudication.answer: Yes. Frozen Intel operating cash forecasts can support an explicit, capital-aware relative SHORT criterion. A fully funded allocation initially matched to the selected historical market beta clears a stated capital hurdle in the central case. This substantively repairs the previously undefined risk-adjusted objective. It does not turn the same cash forecasts into a profitable outright short, establish expected alpha, or make the framework independently validated.
adjudication.recommendation_strength: Moderate, conditional support for an Intel SHORT within a diversified long-short allocation. The selected sustainable-payout ERP method and central capital economics produce an affirmative result without a weaker operating base. The matched plain-cash ERP control, maturing-risk case, and favorable operating case show that the conclusion is method-sensitive. Do not present this as a robust arbitrage or use the positive benchmark assumption as an independently demonstrated edge.
adjudication.economic_decision_rule: For the specified funded positions and cash policies, require terminal net wealth to exceed the opportunity cost of all initial investor capital. At the selected 9.35% benchmark assumption and 3% net short-proceeds yield, the maximum Intel cover compatible with a 4.94% annual capital hurdle is $75.42 at end-2029 and $82.28 at end-2030. Central covers $64.15/$70.98 satisfy that criterion; favorable covers $83.51/$92.58 do not. These thresholds price an explicit judgment rather than assign probability to its success.
adjudication.central_return_attribution: End-2030: the conditional factor-relative cover spread is +$36.58 per $100 short, reduced by $9.12 short-proceeds funding drag, $7.37 own-cash opportunity cost, and $0.68 trading costs, leaving $19.41 above the full-capital hurdle. The actual portfolio has no financing loan. The synthetic attribution benchmark b*GM+(1-b)*GA contains a negative cash weight because b>1; this is an attribution identity, not a claim that borrowing at 4.94% is available.
adjudication.competing_comparators: Cash is an opportunity-cost comparator and has zero market beta; it does not match the strategy company-specific risk. The same SPY and own cash without an Intel short returns 7.10% conditionally versus the strategy 6.43%, and the short reduces wealth by $8.95 per $100 short. That no-short allocation retains greater initial market exposure, so it neither proves nor disproves the short hedging value. Neither comparator warrants a same-risk claim.
adjudication.risk_adjusted_interpretation: The central conditional Intel price CAGR is 4.86% to end-2030. The initially beta-matched market/cash synthetic holding has an equivalent conditional CAGR of 11.70%, under the chosen market/cash assumptions. Their horizon wealth difference is a Jensen-style factor-relative diagnostic, not an empirical alpha estimate, not the operating DCF rate minus share-price CAGR, and not a maintained hedge.
adjudication.not_circular_accounting: The strategy charges the opportunity cost of all investor capital, keeps short proceeds separate, fully funds the SPY long, and incorporates opening/closing costs. The positive result is not produced by spending the same proceeds twice or excluding posted cash. The exact attribution identity and full-capital payoff agree to numerical precision.
adjudication.shared_model_dependency: The 9.35% market return assumption and Intel discount rate share the selected NYU sustainable-payout ERP. This is coherent implementation of one pricing framework; it is not a second independent confirmation of Intel mispricing. Moving both sides to the primary-source plain T12 ERP gives 4.912% strategy CAGR to end-2030 versus 4.94% capital hurdle. That near-zero result is the clearest method-risk objection.
adjudication.what_is_repaired: The return objective, benchmark, initial position sizing, investor-capital denominator, proceeds treatment, cost treatment, horizon, and failure thresholds are now explicit. An initially beta-managed investor can rationally prefer a lower raw return to an unhedged higher-beta allocation; negative standalone short P&L is therefore not a logical veto.
adjudication.what_is_not_repaired: The calculation does not establish that conditional intrinsic values will be the cover prices, that 9.35% will be the finite-horizon market total return, that beta will stay constant, that the selected ERP method is uniquely right, or that a fixed collateral buffer survives every intervening path. Those are genuine investment/model judgments. They cannot be resolved by changing labels or assigning ungrounded scenario weights.
adjudication.not_new_competition_requirements: A specified hedge, an exact consensus miss, a guaranteed catalyst, positive P&L in every case, and numerical scenario weights are not formal M37 requirements. The additional strategy work is a practical repair to this pitch economic ambiguity, not a condition imposed on all valid short pitches.
adjudication.minimum_author_ownership: An affirmative recommendation should explicitly own: why the selected cash-conversion/capital trajectory is a reasonable central judgment; why the sustainable-payout ERP framework is the preferred valuation convention despite plain-cash control; and why the intended portfolio values initial market-risk reduction enough to accept the short leg standalone drag. No new operating assumption is needed merely to state and evaluate that decision.
adjudication.presentation_sentence: SHORT Intel within a diversified long-short allocation: our funded cash-flow case implies about 4.9% annual price appreciation to end-2030, insufficient for its modeled market-risk exposure. A fully funded, initially beta-matched benchmark illustration earns about 6.4% on committed capital under an explicit 9.35% market-return assumption, versus a 4.94% capital hurdle. The matched alternative ERP method reduces that result to roughly the hurdle, which limits conviction.

implementation_and_model_limits: The 260-week INTC/SPY beta is 1.6274 with historical R-squared 0.2209; 104-week beta is 2.1047 and 52-week beta 3.7315. These data justify an observable initial-sizing rule, not a known future beta. They do not remove company-specific risk.

Fixed initial shares produce evolving notionals. Even if beta remained 1.6274, central end-2030 factor exposure is +$36.83 per $100 initial short, or about +0.108 beta on terminal wealth. The portfolio is initially estimated beta-matched, not continuously market neutral.

Maintaining a hedge through time would require a rebalancing rule, paths, transaction costs, and financing estimates. This endpoint analysis does not invent those paths and does not claim execution equivalence to a dynamically hedged fund.

Using an implied market IRR as a constant 3-5-year total-return CAGR requires additional assumptions about cash-flow realization, terminal pricing and reinvestment. Do not add dividends again to the 9.35% total-return assumption.
The 4.94% capital hurdle is the paired long-term NYU Treasury input. It is not an asserted locked 3-5-year Treasury return. A 3.38% broker-cash hurdle and a 6% alternative hurdle are also shown.

The 3% net short-proceeds yield is an illustrative aggregate return after borrow/program costs. Actual credit, stock borrow, collateral marking, margin usage and future rates can differ. A current large-account gross tier illustration is not an actual INTC borrow quote.

Own cash receives the approximate posted marginal 3.38% control, not an exact blended forecast. Short proceeds are not simultaneously used to fund the long. Cash and proceeds are both investor balance-sheet assets offset by the stock liability, but only own contributed capital belongs in K.
No Intel dividend is included, consistent with the retained-cash model. Any future dividend must reduce retained terminal cash and create a short payment together.

Terminal intrinsic value is used as a conditional cover price. A convergence assumption is legitimate in a fundamental pitch when stated and defended, but is not implied automatically by DCF arithmetic.
No probability weights, expected-market-return distribution, realized alpha, risk-free arbitrage, or probability of competition victory is claimed.

M37_scope.requirements: Choose Intel or SpaceX, recommend long or short on fundamental analysis over 3-5 years. Initial PDF at most 10 pages with company overview, drivers and risks. Later memo and Q&A emphasize evidence, valuation, judgment, assumptions and changes of view.
M37_scope.benchmark_context: The published rules do not forbid benchmark or portfolio context and do not mandate a hedge. They select one company; therefore retain Intel as the investment recommendation and use SPY/cash as the implementation and opportunity-cost context. The rules do not explicitly approve a separate two-stock competition entry.
M37_scope.judgment: This relative framework can explain why an Intel short belongs in a portfolio without claiming the stock price must fall. Its acceptability under written scope does not independently establish that the investment is good.

prior_pdf_pages_7_8_check.scope: Read-only text check of nine-page version before this framework was built. Root owns subsequent PDF changes.
prior_pdf_pages_7_8_check.result: No material contradiction found in common-horizon weak/central/favorable price-only short table, net proceeds break-even discussion, or explicit statement that outright multi-year short remains incomplete. The relative framework supplies the previously missing separately justified return criterion, with the limits above.
